ruledBy: FOUNDER DIRECTION 2026-08-18 — keep it explicitly recorded, change nothing.

theAsymmetry.aiOutputReporting: AIReportCategory includes VIOLENCE_OR_SELF_HARM — a person can report an AI response for self-harm content.
theAsymmetry.userContentReporting: The canonical content taxonomy has no dedicated self-harm category. Its nearest neighbour, VIOLENCE_OR_THREAT, covers threats to OTHERS — harm directed outward, not inward.
theAsymmetry.currentBehaviour: User-content self-harm material reaches OTHER when no existing governed category applies.
theAsymmetry.whyItIsNotAMappingProblem: VIOLENCE_OR_THREAT and VIOLENCE_OR_SELF_HARM share the word VIOLENCE and are close to disjoint in meaning. Treating one as covering the other would be exactly the false equivalence the taxonomy-relationship ruling forbids.

explicitlyNotDone: SELF_HARM was NOT added to the content taxonomy.
The two taxonomies were NOT merged.
Self-harm was NOT artificially mapped onto VIOLENCE_OR_THREAT or any other category.
AIReportCategory is NOT treated as authority for ordinary content.
No current reporting behaviour was changed.
enforcement: src/moderation/taxonomy-relationship.spec.ts fails if a future contributor adds SELF_HARM or MISINFORMATION to the content taxonomy without a governed policy change. The asymmetry cannot be quietly closed by inference.
natureOfTheQuestion: This is a substantive moderation-policy question — whether Aura offers a first-class route to report self-harm material about a person — not taxonomy normalisation. It belongs to CH-15 / content-safety policy adjudication.

blockingStatus.condition: Return it for ruling only when a concrete executable unit actually requires it — for example when CH-15's report journey is constructed and the category set becomes a build input.

visibility: aura-backend/src/moderation/taxonomy-relationship.ts — COVERAGE_ASYMMETRIES, first entry, marked the most safety-relevant
